newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bonds end up, Rally's Hamburgers gain.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bonds end up, Rally's Hamburgers gain.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds across the credit spectrum closed near session highs and Rally's Hamburgers debt jumped on news the firm solicited bondholders to try and avoid a change-of-control put at 101, dealers said.

Rally's said on Thursday it is seeking consent from bondholders to amend the indenture to allow two equity holders to acquire a 35 percent stake in the company without triggering the existing change of control provisions.
These provisions require the company to offer to purchase the senior notes at 101 percent of their face value, Rally's said.
Rally's Hamburgers 9.875 percent notes due 2000 closed up 3-1/2 points at 87-1/4 bid, 87-1/2 offer, but were quoted as much as five points higher in Thursday's session, high-yield traders said.

In other news, the unwinding of Kohlberg, Kravis, Roberts & Co L.P.'s plans to acquire Xerox's Talegen Holding Inc spurred Talegen Acquisition Corp to pull it's planned $350 million issue of senior subordinated debentures due 2008.
Merrill Lynch & Co Inc was the lead manager.
Talegen Acquisition was formed by the buyout specialist KKR to partly finance the agreed $2.7 billion purchase of Talegen Holding, a commercial property and casualty insurance firm, from Xerox Corp.
In the overall market, dealers quoted spreads to Treasuries in high-grades unchanged. The 30-year long bond closed up 14/32 at 95-31/32 to yield 7.08 percent.
Meanwhile, junk bonds closed up 1/8 to 1/4 of a point, dealers said.
The primary market saw a return of issuance, with four deals pricing, as syndicate calendars build.
Anixter Inc priced $100 million seven-year notes to yield 135 basis points over Treasuries via Merrill.
Comerica's priced $150 million in 30-year debt to yield 85 basis points over Treasuries via CS First Boston.
Associates Corp of North America priced $400 million in three-year notes to yield 26 basis points over U.S. Treasuries via Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Lastly, Pearson Inc priced $250 million in 10-year medium-term notes rated A1/A-plus at a 63 basis point spread via Merrill.
Wednesday's numerous large yankee new issues held their own after being freed to trade on Thursday, dealers said.
European Investment Bank's 10-year global bonds were seen trading at a bid spread of 17 basis points, where the paper initially priced.
Australia & New Zealand Banking's 10-year issue via Merrill Lynch & Co traded at a spread of 64 bid, 63 offer point spread on the break, matching the new issue price.
